title.narrative: Ensuring Inclusiveness and Service Delivery for Persons with Disabilities Project

description.narrative: Often, public support to persons with disabilities (PWDs) focus on providing assistance under the concept of social welfare. However, this project will highlight what PWDs can do to ensure inclusion of PWDs in society, including them in mainstream economic activities, creating opportunities in education and employment, and providing access to the services they need. It will strengthen and institutionalize early identification of disability; improve service delivery and access to the physical environment; improve employment prospects; and contribute to strategic development for PWDs, including social welfare reform, awareness raising, and attitude change.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Access to services and employment for PWDs increased

90% of CWDs enrolled in a portage program receive at least one other service in project areas (sex disaggregated) (2016 baseline: not applicable) Progress/Status: Being implemented. - Regulations on the Portage program- the model of interactive parent-child-facilitator education in early childhood was developed, and implementation in five DCs in project aimags commenced in Q1 2024. - In Q3 2022, 50 Portage teachers were trained in six aimags. Re-training conducted in 3Q 2024. - Construction of five Development Centers (DC) for PWD in project aimags completed in Q4 2023. Data Source: MLSP's MIS to be developed in new development and rehabilitation centers, and records from children's disability commissions (annual, once established) Actual value:

Number of employed PWDs increased by 1,500 at least 50% of whom are women (sex disaggregated) (2014 baseline: 24,720) Progress/Status: Being implemented. - In 2024, 31,072 PWD were employed out of 94,24 adult PWD. A total of 1456 PWD (576 or 39.5% are women) are working in the civil service sector. Data Source: Annual NSO labor force survey reports Actual value:

Companies employing at least one PWD by quota increased to 50% (2013 baseline: 29%) Progress/Status: Being implemented. Baseline survey (2020) results reveal that companies employing at least one PWD by quota are 76%, of which in project sites 84.4% and in Ulaanbaatar 67.1%. The end-line survey is ongpong. Data Source: Surveys commissioned by the PIU and DPOs (beginning and end of project) Actual value:

PWDs and parents of CWDs satisfied or very satisfied with public services increased to more than 50% (sex disaggregated) (2016 indicative baseline: 40% in Ulaanbaatar) Progress/Status: Being implemented. The baseline survey of 2020 reveals that PWDs are satisfied with public services in project sites: - Ulaanbaatar: 43.3% (46% women) - Project 6 aimags: 60.5% (66.3% women) Parents of CWD satisfied with public services in project sites: - Ulaanbaatar: 34 % (46.5% women) - Project 6 aimags: 61% (56.2% women) The end-line survey is ongoing, to be completed in Q1, 2026. Data Source: PIU survey of PWDs in 2021 and 2025 Actual value:
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: 2. Service delivery for PWDs improved Indicator: 12 multidisciplinary teams working with new MLSP standard operating procedures in project areas (2016 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Consultant C2 is assisting in improving the functions of the multisectoral commissions responsible for the disability assessment of children. They provided recommendations on the commission structure, tasks, and job description for commission members and developed operational guidelines and procedures and M&E. Based on recommendations, in 2021, the MLSP, MES, and MOH jointly approved a decree (A/220, A/475, A/812 of 30 December 2021) to endorse revised guidelines and methodology for the development assessment and assistance for CWD to be used by multisectoral commissions. In 2022, the project trained members of the multisectoral commission in project aimags and Ulaanbaatar on newly approved guidelines and methodology. Data Source: MLSP project reports Actual value:

Output: 3. Access to the physical environment improved Indicator: Government websites that are made user-friendly for PWD or similar increased by 50% (2016 baseline: none) Progress/Status: To improve accessibility to visually impaired people, MLSP initiated the development of the Mongolian text-speech (TTS) software system. The software was completed in 2023 and accepted by MFLSP in June 2024. It is open-source and will be installed on government websites. MFLSP decided to transfer the software to the Ministry of Digital Development, Innovations and Communications for the future development and make government e-platform to be accessible. MDDIC accepted the request and directed E-Mongolia Academy to receive to software and be responsible for future updates regarding the software. Data Source: Reports commissioned by the PIU and DPOs (beginning and end of project) Actual value:

Output: 4. Work and employment for PWDs improved Indicator: Number of PWD job seekers provided skills development and job matching and brokering support by public employment services increased to 400 (2016 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: In 2021, 271 PWD-job seekers were provided skills development and job matching support by public employment services. - Consultant C3 developed a partnership and cooperation model between the employment promotion services run by DPOs and the public employment promotion services, focusing on job coaching and job brokering services for PWD. Data Source: MLSP's MIS in public employment services (annual) Actual value:

Output: 4. Work and employment for PWDs improved Indicator: Number of PWDs supported by DPOs using new employment service approaches increased to 300, at least 120 of whom are women (sex disaggregated) (2016 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: As of June 2022, there were 1504 PWDs involved in the national program on supporting PWD employment; out of them, 622 were provided with permanent employment. The Project constructed the Employment Resource Center (ERC) for PWD in Ulaanbaatar. The construction of ERC commenced in May 2022 and completed in June 2024. Project Consultant assisted in developing a business plan and development strategy, including organizational management structure and HR for the ERC, and developed service delivery design, operation plans for service units, and job descriptions for ERC staff. Currently the ERC is fully functional and provides employment promotion services with the participation of DPOs, such as assessing the workability of disabled persons and job coaching that is implemented by DPOs and financed by Employment promotion fund. At end of 2025, in total 210 PWDs were evaluated by the ERC. Data Source: MLSP's new MIS module developed for contracting DPOs (annual) Actual value:

Output: 5. Strategic development to support PWDs implemented Indicator: Access to social welfare benefits for PWDs simplified and amount of benefit linked to the three levels of support needs of PWDs by the end of the project increased by 60% (baseline: not applicable) Progress/Status: Consultants C3 reviewed Mongolia's existing social welfare system and international practices on disability allowances and community-based social welfare services. Consultants are working on proposals that require changes in laws and regulations to reform the social welfare system to improve targeting and financial support for PWD. The project prepared the TOR for consultancy service (C27) to undertake the remaining assignments from the C3 contract to assist the EA in developing the proposal on regulatory changes in social welfare sector. In October 2024, MFLSP established the Consultant Selection Committee on recruitment of the candidate for this consultancy assignment. Due to budget restriction by MOF, this consultancy service has been postponed to 2026. Data Source: MLSP's new regulations prepared and approved (ad hoc) Actual value:

Output: 5. Strategic development to support PWDs implemented Indicator: Every child assessed by the medical commissions in project areas has an ICF diagnosis completed (sex disaggregated) (2016 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Consultants C3 reviewed the existing policies, institutional arrangements, and human resources required for introducing and implementing the International Classification of Functioning, Disability, and Health (ICF) in multi-sectoral commissions. They proposed a simplified ICF model for assessing the workability of PWD. MLSP, jointly with MOH, pilot-tested the simplified ICF tools in 2022. The government decision on nationwide usage of the simplified ICF is pending. Consultants prepared a training program on ICF assessment tools for members of multi-sectoral commissions in six project sites. In February 2024, the project consultants conducted training sessions in Ulaanbaatar in Darkhan-Uul with 84 participants and tested the assessment tools with the help of 20 PWD. In September 2024, the EA organized a consultative meeting with relevant stakeholders on the proposed assessment tools. Data Source: General Authority for Social Insurance and MLSP internal reports and project documentation (annual) Actual value:

Output: 5. Strategic development to support PWDs implemented Indicator: Media content on disability rights and issues reaching target audiences and meeting quality criteria set by DPOs increased by 40% (baseline: not applicable) Progress/Status: A media monitoring survey was conducted in December 2021. Out of 200 PWDs who participated in the survey, 71.4 percent were satisfied with the visual presentation of published articles and the needs of PWDs. - MLSP approved the Communication Strategy for awareness-raising and attitude change towards PWD and the Action Plan for its implementation. The awareness-raising communication campaign will go through three main channels: public events and national campaigns, TV and radio programs, and mass media advertisements. - In 2021, MLSP signed contracts with seven national firms and DPOs to develop the content of awareness-raising programs with the participation of PWD. As of 1 October 2022, there are 102 newspaper contents developed and published (articles, interviews, editorials, and discussions in the daily newspaper “Today”), 40 television programs (20 min), 22 short video spots (30 sec), and 8 radio contents developed and broadcasted. Production of social content on the rights of PWDs, social protection, and employment opportunities is ongoing. Data Source: PIU media monitoring and audience research (annual) Actual value:

Output: 2. Service delivery for PWDs improved Indicator: Eight PWD development and rehabilitation centers according to universal design specifications built or constructed (2017 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: MLSP contracted six civil construction companies to build DCs for PWD in the project aimags. Construction work commenced in June 2021 and was completed in Q4 2023. Procurement of equipment for six DCs, including furniture, assistive technology, IT, and orthopedic equipment, has been completed. Except for Arkhangai aimag, 5 DCs commenced rehabilitation, habilitation, and social services for PWDs. OTs, PTs, and AT technicians are in shortage in local provinces, yet 90% of the required staff were recruited.
In Arkhangai aimag, the working team of the MFLSP decided to extend the contract with the same contractor and agreed to complete the construction by September 2025. As of 1 October 2025, the construction progress is 87%. The Contract was expired on 1 December 2025. As of 31 Dec 2025, construction progress is 95% and the state commissioning is planned on 6 February 2026 to be established by the Governor of Arkhangai aimag. In the Bayanzurkh district, one household was affected by resettlement. The MFLSP prepared a due diligence report and started implementing the corrective action plan for the affected household, which were reviewed and endorsed by ADB. The MFLSP awarded contract for construction of DC in Bayanzurkh district in October 2025. After contract signing on 29 October 2025, the construction work was started and current progress is 5%. Construction work will resume on 1 April 2026.
New DC for PWD in Zavkhan aimag, the geological survey has been completed, the site-specific due diligence has been conducted, which was reviewed by ADB. The civil work procurement started in March 2025 but failed twice. The rebidding for the 3rd time is advertised on 24 July 2025 and MFLSP awarded a contract for construction of DC in Zavkhan Province on 11 December 2025. Construction work will start from 1 April 2026. Data Source: MLSP project reports Actual value:

Output: 3. Access to the physical environment improved Indicator: PWDs who receive assistive devices in project areas increased to 15% for both men and women (sex disaggregated) (2016 indicative baseline: 6%) Progress/Status: According to the baseline survey conducted in 2020, 39.4% (44.6% women) are satisfied with the quality and comfort of assistive devices. An endline survey is ongoing.
To ensure increased access to AT and prostheses, the project upgraded the capacity of the Orthopedic and Prosthesis Factory, the only factory in the country that makes prostheses and orthopedic goods. The project built a new ventilation system, procured equipment and spare parts for existing Ottobock machines (61 types, 201 pieces, $425,510), and completed electrical repair work of the central 380 kW power to ensure proper operation of the orthopedic factory. All equipment has been installed, and the orthopedic factory is fully operational.
The project upgraded the capacity of the Vocational Training Center for PWD. It procured AT equipment and tools for training courses (72 types, 430 pieces, $175,126), which were delivered in November 2023. Data Source: NSO, household socioeconomic survey biennial reports, PIU survey of PWDs in 2021 and 2025 Actual value:

Output: 1. Early identification of CWDs strengthened and institutionalized Indicator: Early identification model of CWDs in MLSP initiated and implemented (2016 baseline: not initiated) Progress/Status: The MLSP engaged the consultant MCDS Consultancy LLC (C2) in 2019 to develop a modified ASQ screening system for the early identification of disabilities in young children. Consultant C2 recommended the Mongolian Rapid Baby Scale (MORBAS) to screen 0-42-month-old infants by primary-level medical doctors. The early screening questionnaire of the MORBAS was reviewed by the TWG, established by MLSP and MOH in April 2022. The MORBAS and modified Pink Book were approved by the Ministry of Health on 29 Sep 2023. For assessing child development delays, consultant C2 recommended using the Dr. Baumann approach instead of BSID (planned at the project appraisal), which was mutually agreed upon by MLSP and MOH. Dr.Bauman's assessment tool will be introduced at the referral level national centers and secondary level aimag/district hospitals. MLSP, MES, and MOH approved a joint decree A/220, A/475, and A/812 in December 2021 to approve the methodology and forms for providing comprehensive development support to CWD. A handbook on using the Pink Book has been prepared. The PIU conducted ToT training (201 participants). The nationwide training for primary-level medical staff (1200 people) in all provinces and cities has been completed in March 2025. MLSP signed a contract with Dr. Baumann to provide i) a tool for assessment examination ii) training for health professionals, and iii) hearing, plus optic devices and a testing toolkit set. The service commenced in May 2023. Online training (50 hours) for pediatricians from the National Center for Maternal and Child Health and aimag general hospitals was conducted in May 2024 and followed by a 4-days in-class practical training by Dr.Bauman and his team for 30 pediatricians in September 2024. In total, 1300 health personnel were prepared through 10 sessions on modified Child Health and Development Book (Pink Book). Nationwide training session of primary-level medical doctors on early identification has been completed.
Data Source: Ministry of Health modified reporting as part of project activities (annual, once monitoring system is established) Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Target year: 2027 Target value: Y

Output: 2. Service delivery for PWDs improved Indicator: PWD-dedicated hotline on information, counselling, and referrals (for PWDs) established (2016 baseline: not established) Progress/Status: In June 2021, MLSP established the Social Protection Call Center with specific modules for communicating and providing information for people with hearing impairment. The project supported the local service providers' purchasing service fee for a three-year subscription in connecting to the state inter-sectoral web platform www.duudlaga.mn. As of October 2023, 77835 calls were received and responded to. Data Source: MLSP project reports Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Target year: 2027 Target value: Y

Output: 3. Access to the physical environment improved Indicator: Standards for accessibility harmonized with health and safety standards and made widely available to decision makers (baseline: not applicable) Progress/Status: Project Consultant developed recommendations to improve legislation, regulations, and accessibility-related standards for construction, road and transportation, information communication, health, and social services. They also provided recommendations for revision of (i) the Law on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (2016) and (ii) the National Program on the Rights, Inclusiveness, and Support for PWD. Consultants assisted MLSP in drafting a new bill on improving the accessibility for disabled people (Bill on Barrier-free and Accessible Environment for PWD). Consultant also reviewed the current situation with the accessibility audit to identify accessibility barriers, developed tools for conducting the accessibility audit, and prepared a report with findings from a comparison of the 2015, 2020, and 2022 accessibility audits conducted by Universal Development NGO. MFLSP established working group to develop regulatory documents based on project consultants' reports and recommendations. However, due to frequent changes in the government, there is little or no progress. Data Source: PIU documentation and training reports (ad hoc) Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Target year: 2027 Target value: Y

Output: 5. Strategic development to support PWDs implemented Indicator: NSO statistics capture disability levels based on functioning aligned with the Washington Group on Disability Statistics questions and routinely provide sex-disaggregated statistics on PWDs (2016 baseline: none) Progress/Status: MLSP organized an extensive consultation meeting with NSO to follow up on the C7 consultant's recommendation for the integration database on disability statistics. - MLSP, GADPWD, and NSO developed the action plan to create a data system for disability statistics. - The Joint Technical Working Group was established by the Joint Order A112/A87 of the MLSP and NSO dated 27 May 2022 to create the integrated database on PWDs by organizing consultation meetings, developing the methodological tools, forms, and indicators, learning international practices on PWD statistics. Data Source: NSO annual publications Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Target year: 2027 Target value: Y

Output: Project Management Indicator: Project is implemented satisfactory Progress/Status: Being implemented in compliance with the LA, GA, PAM and MOF Regulation No. 4. Data Source: MLSP project reports Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y
